title: Terms of Use and Health Disclaimer

sections.heading: 1. What FitnessLab is
paragraphs: FitnessLab is a free demonstration project built to showcase software engineering practice. It is published as an open-source portfolio piece.
It is not a commercial product, not a medical device, and not a health service. It is not operated by a company, and there is no support desk behind it.

sections.heading: 2. No professional qualifications, no medical advice
paragraphs: The person who built FitnessLab is a software developer. They are not a doctor, dietitian, nutritionist, physiotherapist, or certified personal trainer, and hold no qualification in medicine, nutrition, or fitness.

Everything this application produces — BMI values, weight categories, training plans, meal plans, and calorie figures — is generated by simple, hard-coded rules written to demonstrate programming techniques. These outputs are not medical, nutritional, dietary, or fitness advice; are not tailored to your health status, medical history, medication, injuries, allergies, or individual circumstances; have not been reviewed or approved by any qualified professional; and must not be used to diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any condition.
Consult a qualified healthcare professional before changing your diet, starting an exercise programme, or acting on anything you see here.

sections.heading: 3. Limitations of BMI
paragraphs: BMI is a crude population-level statistic, not an individual health assessment. It is calculated only from height and weight, and therefore cannot distinguish muscle from fat, or account for body composition, frame size, fat distribution, age, or ethnicity.

BMI is particularly unreliable, and its categories should not be applied, for: children and adolescents under 18, for whom age- and sex-specific growth charts are required instead; people who are pregnant or breastfeeding; athletes and people with high muscle mass, who are routinely misclassified as overweight; and older adults, and people with conditions affecting body composition or fluid balance.
A BMI figure alone says nothing conclusive about any individual's health.

sections.heading: 4. Please take care of yourself
paragraphs: If you have, or think you may have, an eating disorder or a difficult relationship with food, weight, or exercise, tools that display weight categories and calorie targets can be harmful. This application is a programming demonstration and is not designed with any clinical safeguards. Please consider not using it, and speak to a healthcare professional or a support organisation in your country.

Do not use this application to restrict calories below levels a qualified professional has advised, and stop exercising and seek medical attention if you experience pain, dizziness, chest discomfort, or breathing difficulty.

sections.heading: 5. Intended users
paragraphs: FitnessLab is intended for adults aged 18 or over. Accounts should not be created by anyone under 18. As noted above, BMI categories are not valid for under-18s in any case.

sections.heading: 6. It is free
paragraphs: FitnessLab is provided free of charge. There are no paid tiers, no subscriptions, no payment processing, no advertising, and no sale or sharing of user data. Nothing on this site is an offer to sell anything.

sections.heading: 7. Your account and your data
paragraphs: Creating an account is optional — the BMI calculator on the landing page works without one, and calculations made there are not stored on the server.

If an account is created, the data stored is: name, email address, password (stored only as a secure hash), preferred language, and the measurements, plans, and check-offs created within the application.

What this means under the GDPR: body weight and BMI, linked to an identifiable person, may be treated as data concerning health — a special category under Article 9. This application handles them on the basis of your explicit consent, given when you choose to create an account and enter them. Consent can be withdrawn at any time by deleting your account, which removes the account and all data associated with it. Data is stored on a server in the European Union and is not sold, shared, or transferred to third parties.

You may request access to your data, its correction, or its deletion by contacting the address in section 12. The simplest route is to delete your account from the application, which does the same thing immediately.

Separately from your account, the application keeps short-lived technical error logs so that faults can be diagnosed. These may incidentally include an email address or an identifier if an error occurred while you were using the site. Passwords and access tokens are stripped before anything is written, the logs are readable only by the site administrator, and entries are deleted automatically after a short retention period.
The minimum-data principle applies to you too: please do not enter more than you need to try the application out. Nothing here requires real data.

Because this is a demonstration project, no guarantee is made about data retention, backups, or availability. Data may be lost, and the demo may be reset or taken offline without notice. Do not store anything here that matters to you.

sections.heading: 7a. The demo account
paragraphs: A shared demo account is provided so the application can be explored without registering. It is public: anyone can sign in to it, and anything entered there is visible to everyone else using it. Its contents are wiped and reset to seeded sample data on a nightly schedule.
Never enter real or personal information into the demo account.

sections.heading: 8. Provided "as is"
paragraphs: FitnessLab is provided "as is" and "as available", without warranty of any kind, express or implied — including any warranty of accuracy, merchantability, or fitness for a particular purpose.
No promise is made that the application will be available, uninterrupted, error-free, or that its output is correct. It may be modified, suspended, or discontinued at any time without notice.

sections.heading: 9. Limitation of liability
paragraphs: To the fullest extent permitted by applicable law, the author of FitnessLab accepts no liability for any loss, injury, or damage — including any health consequence — arising from use of, or reliance on, this application or anything it generates.
You use FitnessLab entirely at your own risk. Nothing in these terms limits liability that cannot be limited by law.

paragraphs: The source code is published under the MIT licence and is available in the project repository. The MIT licence covers the code only; it grants no endorsement of the application's output and does not alter the disclaimers above.

sections.heading: 11. Changes
paragraphs: These terms may change as the project develops. The current version is always the one published in the repository, with the date shown at the top.

sections.heading: 12. Contact
paragraphs: Questions about these terms, or requests concerning your data, can be sent to fitnesslab@zaitis.dev. This is a personal project, so replies are not guaranteed to be prompt.
